description: 50 original OC-friendly geometric reasoning questions with deterministic answer-key proofs

questions.name: Symmetry and Reflection
questions.text: Which option shows the vertical mirror image of the coloured-dot pattern?
questions.imageAlt: A four-by-four grid of coloured dots with a vertical dashed mirror axis and four answer grids labelled A to D.
questions.tip: Follow each coloured dot across the dashed mirror line. Keep its distance from the line unchanged.
questions.explanation: Imagine reflecting the pattern across a vertical mirror. Every coloured dot moves to the other side of the line by the same distance; its colour and height stay the same. Option C is the exact reflection.

questions.explanation: Imagine reflecting the pattern across a horizontal mirror. Every coloured dot moves to the other side of the line by the same distance; its colour and left-to-right position stay the same. Option D is the exact reflection.

questions.name: Matching Figures
questions.text: Which figure is an exact match to the reference, without turning or flipping it?
questions.imageAlt: A four-by-four tile pattern of six coloured geometric symbols and four answer grids labelled A to D, including rotations and reflections.
questions.tip: Compare the exact positions of each symbol. Do not rotate or flip the reference.
questions.explanation: The correct figure must keep all the different shapes in precisely the same positions. Option C matches the original without any rotation or reflection.

questions.name: Simple Visual Patterns
questions.text: Which arrow comes next in the picture sequence?
questions.imageAlt: Three successive coloured arrows that turn a quarter-turn and alternate colour, followed by a missing tile and four labelled arrow options.
questions.tip: Look for both the arrow direction and the alternating colour.
questions.explanation: Each arrow makes a quarter-turn clockwise, while its colour alternates between two colours. The next arrow therefore has the direction and colour in option B.

questions.name: Odd One Out
questions.text: Three cards show dots on a straight line. Which is different?
questions.imageAlt: Four cards with three-by-three dot grids labelled A to D. Three follow the rule of three dots forming a straight line, and one differs.
questions.tip: Check which figure follows the same visual rule as the other three.
questions.explanation: Options other than C place all their dark dots along one straight line. Option C forms a bent L-shape, so it is the odd one out.

questions.name: Odd One Out
questions.text: Three cards have vertical symmetry. Which card is different?
questions.imageAlt: Four cards with three-by-three dot grids labelled A to D. Three follow the rule of vertical symmetry, and one differs.
questions.tip: Check which figure follows the same visual rule as the other three.
questions.explanation: In the other three cards, the dots match across the central vertical line. Option D has an unpaired dot and does not have vertical symmetry.

questions.imageAlt: A grid of sixteen distinct coloured geometric shapes containing triangles, squares, circles and pentagons, with answer options A to D showing four possible counts.
questions.tip: Count only the requested shape, including differently oriented examples.
questions.explanation: Check the picture row by row and count only the triangles. There are 3, so option A is correct.
